note.question: How should one schedule arrivals at a mass vaccination center to minimize a tri-objective function of (a) the expected number of infections acquired while waiting, (b) throughput, and (c) overtime?
note.overview: Mass vaccination is essential for epidemic control, but long queues can increase infection risk. This paper studies how to schedule arrivals at a mass vaccination center to minimize a tri-objective function of (a) the expected number of infections acquired while waiting, (b) throughput, and (c) overtime. Leveraging multimodularity results of a related optimization problem, we construct a solution algorithm and apply it to a case study of COVID-19.

components.formal: Algorithmic rule: With Proposition 1, we can apply the local search algorithm described in Kaandorp and Koole (2007) to obtain a globally optimal solution for OPT-OVERLAP2.
conditions: Note that OPT-OVERLAP is a constrained optimization problem with the constraint PT i=1 xi = m (as well as the nonnegativity constraints).

The key idea of the algorithm is to start with a feasible schedule, x, and check whether any “neighboring feasible point” (where the neighborhood is determined by the set of vectors used in the multimodularity definition), y, is such that O(y) < O(x).
